title: When the Spire Falls
premise: Paloma Dravenmoor, a beast-speaker who has spent his life passing as an ordinary guild clerk, keeps the ledgers of the Vellum & Thorn, a guild that trades in impossible things—bottled echoes, captive dreams, one stolen star. When the border wards collapse and every star in the sky goes dark on the same night, Paloma learns the guild's founder sealed the stars away to hide a truth: that beast-speakers were made by the old war's last magic, and the wards fed on their voices. Hunted by a moon-cult that wants him as a key and sheltered by the ragtag found family of the guild, Paloma must choose between restoring the stars and unbinding the ancient war. In the end he speaks the forbidden word aloud before the thirteenth moon turns—not to reignite the war, but to end it, giving up his own memories of belonging so his family can keep theirs.
about_author: Ada Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one ever claimed. She writes fantasy about quiet people keeping loud secrets, and lives near a lighthouse she refuses to explain.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A night of routine bookkeeping at the Vellum & Thorn guild: cataloguing bottled echoes and a caged dream, while concealing the fact that he can hear the guild's raven gossiping about him. Establishes his invisibility strategy and his quiet affection for the guild's misfits. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons on the Wall
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The guild's cartographer, Brannic, shows Paloma an old mural of thirteen moons; the thirteenth is scratched out. Paloma's gift lets him hear the building itself hum uneasily. He dismisses it as superstition. Emotional beat: the first crack in his belief that secrets can stay buried forever.

chapters.title: A Buyer for Silence
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A veiled stranger offers the guild an obscene sum for 'a voice that speaks to beasts.' Guildmaster Odessa Vell declines coldly, but Paloma realizes someone knows what he is. That night he confesses nothing to anyone. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into paranoia.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Mid-auction, every star vanishes and the border wards fall with a sound like breaking glass. Animals across the city scream in a language only Paloma understands: they are mourning. The guild locks its doors. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Raven Knew
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, brief interlude from the raven Quillfeather. The raven reveals she has always known Paloma's secret and kept it out of loyalty. She tells him the animals say the stars didn't die—they were taken. Emotional beat: unexpected kinship; Paloma is less alone than he believed.

chapters.title: Odessa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Guildmaster Odessa admits the guild was founded to guard something beneath the spire: the First Voice, the source of all beast-speech. She asks Paloma to help seal it again before the moon-cult finds it. He agrees, lying about why. Emotional beat: trust extended on both sides, both withholding truths.

chapters.title: The Cult of the Open Sky
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Brannic is captured briefly by moon-cultists who preach that the stars must stay extinguished until the 'Speaker' opens the spire. He escapes but brings back a name: Paloma's mother's name, spoken like a prophecy. Emotional beat: protective fury; Brannic chooses family over safety.

chapters.title: Ledgers of the Dead
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Digging through the guild's oldest ledgers, Paloma finds entries in his mother's handwriting—she was the guild's previous keeper and hid him here deliberately. His whole invisible life was designed by someone who loved him. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude tangled together.

chapters.title: The Dream in the Cage
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The guild's caged dream escapes during a cult raid and floods the shop with shared visions: everyone glimpses each other's worst memories, including Paloma's. The found family sees his secret—and stays anyway. Emotional beat: exposure as the beginning of belonging.

chapters.title: Wolves at the Wardline
chapters.summary: Quillfeather's POV and Paloma's. Beast refugees pour toward the city as wild magic leaks through the fallen wards. Paloma must speak publicly to calm a panicked wolf-pack, nearly revealing himself before hundreds of witnesses. Emotional beat: the cost of hiding rising against the instinct to help.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Astronomers confirm the dark moon will complete its thirteenth turn in weeks; when it does, the seal on the First Voice dissolves permanently. Odessa begins training Paloma in the sealing rites—but the rites require a speaker willing to be silenced forever. Emotional beat: dawning sacrifice.

chapters.title: A Stolen Star
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. The guild's most dangerous inventory item—one captured star—is missing from the vaults. Evidence points inside: apprentice Sef has been feeding information to the cult to buy medicine for her sick brother. Emotional beat: betrayal understood, if not forgiven.

chapters.title: The Price of Medicine
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef's chapter: her brother is dying because the fallen wards poisoned the water, and the cult promised a cure. Paloma, instead of turning her in, uses his gift to ask the city's rats where clean water still flows. Emotional beat: mercy as strategy and as love.

chapters.title: Into the Hollow Country
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The guild travels beyond the broken wards to recover the stolen star from the cult's stronghold, guided by beasts who owe Paloma favors. The land outside is memory-blighted: travelers forget their names as they walk. Emotional beat: the theme made landscape—memory as home.

chapters.title: The Speaker Before Me
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In the blight, Paloma encounters the ghost-echo of his mother, preserved in a bottled echo the cult looted. She tells him the truth: the First Voice doesn't start wars—it remembers them, and whoever holds it chooses which memory the world keeps. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed as choice.

chapters.title: Storming the Moonrise Court
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation (Brannic, Sef, Quillfeather). The guild assaults the cult's stronghold during a ritual. Brannic holds a bridge alone; Sef turns her knowledge against her former handlers; Quillfeather carries the recovered star through arrow-fire. Emotional beat: each member risking everything for a family that chose them.

chapters.title: What the Cult Wanted
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Confronting the cult's leader, Paloma learns she is not a fanatic but the last survivor of a people the old war erased—she wants the world to forget the war entirely, even if forgetting erases beast-speakers too. Emotional beat: an enemy with a grief that mirrors his own.

chapters.title: The Spire Opens
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. On the twelfth turn, the seal fails early—the cult's stolen star destabilized it. Paloma descends into the spire's heart and stands before the First Voice, which speaks to him in every animal tongue at once, offering to carry any memory he gives it. Emotional beat: terror and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Word That Ends Wars
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Climax. Instead of resealing the Voice or surrendering his people's memory, Paloma speaks the forbidden word aloud—a word that makes the First Voice remember the war's ending rather than its beginning. The stars reignite; the moon-cult leader, shown her people remembered with honor instead of shame, stands down. But the word demands payment: Paloma's own memories of belonging. Emotional beat: triumph purchased with self-erasure.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Table
chapters.summary: Guild ensemble POV. Paloma wakes with no memory of the guild, the family, or his gift—only ledgers in his own hand proving he was loved. The others refuse to let him remain a stranger: Brannic retells every story, Sef replays the escaped dream's visions, Quillfeather simply refuses to leave his shoulder. Emotional beat: found family rebuilding what magic took.

chapters.title: Beast-Speaker
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The gift returns fragmentarily—not erased after all, only sleeping, because the First Voice chose to return it as a debt of honor. Paloma hears the raven first, then the wolves, then, faintly, the city itself saying his name. He stops hiding. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed, publicly and without apology.

chapters.title: When the Spire Falls
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, epilogue. The guild deliberately dismantles the spire—no more seals, no more hidden voices—and rebuilds it as an open school where speakers and non-speakers learn together under restored stars. Paloma writes the final ledger entry: not an inventory of impossible things, but a list of names. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, kept, and given away freely.
